---
title: "Navbars, Page Footers, and Prev/Next Navigation"
---

Quarto 2 lets a single HTML document declare its own top-level navbar,
page footer, and prev/next page navigation through YAML metadata, using
the same mental model as the table of contents. Configuration can live in
the document's frontmatter, in a directory `_metadata.yml`, or in
`_quarto.yml`; the usual metadata-merge rules resolve conflicts.

## Navbar

The `navbar:` key controls the top navigation bar. In its simplest form you
provide items for the `left` and `right` sides, along with a title:

``` yaml
---
title: My Document
navbar:
  title: Navbar Demo Site
  background: primary
  search: true
  left:
    - text: Home
      href: index.qmd
    - text: Docs
      menu:
        - text: Getting Started
          href: start.qmd
        - text: Reference
          href: ref.qmd
  right:
    - icon: github
      href: https://github.com/
      aria-label: GitHub
---
```

### Navbar options

| Option             | Description                                                                                                 |
|--------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `title`            | Brand text. Defaults to the document's `title`. Use `false` to hide.                                        |
| `logo`             | Path to a logo image displayed left of the title.                                                           |
| `logo-alt`         | Alternate text for the logo.                                                                                |
| `logo-href`        | Link target for the logo/title (defaults to `/`).                                                           |
| `background`       | Background color: a Bootstrap named color (`primary`, `secondary`, …, `light`, `dark`) or a hex value.      |
| `foreground`       | Foreground color for navbar text.                                                                           |
| `search`           | `true` to emit a search placeholder that theme JS can wire up.                                              |
| `pinned`           | `true` to keep the navbar visible when scrolling.                                                           |
| `collapse`         | `false` to disable the hamburger collapse behavior (default `true`).                                        |
| `collapse-below`   | Breakpoint for collapsing: `sm`, `md`, `lg` (default), `xl`, `xxl`.                                         |
| `toggle-position`  | `left` (default) or `right` for the hamburger toggle.                                                       |
| `tools-collapse`   | Whether tool icons collapse into the menu at narrow widths.                                                 |
| `left`             | List of navigation items for the left side.                                                                 |
| `right`            | List of navigation items for the right side.                                                                |

### Disabling the navbar

Use `navbar: false` to suppress the navbar — for example, in a specific
document that should opt out of a project-wide navbar.

## Page navigation (prev/next)

Long websites and books often want a "previous / next" strip at the
bottom of each page so readers can move through the content without
jumping back to the sidebar. Quarto 2 emits this as a `<nav class=
"page-navigation">` containing two anchors styled into a single row,
left-aligned for the previous page and right-aligned for the next.

### Enabling

Page navigation is **off by default for websites** — matching Quarto 1
— and on by default for books (currently unreachable in Quarto 2 but
the hook is wired). Opt in by setting `page-navigation: true` at one
of these layers:

``` yaml
# _quarto.yml — top level
page-navigation: true

# _quarto.yml — under website:
website:
  page-navigation: true
```

Both placements have the same effect; the top-level form composes
naturally with document-frontmatter overrides through Quarto 2's
metadata merge.

### Per-document overrides

Set `page-navigation` in a document's frontmatter to override the
project default for that page:

``` yaml
---
title: My Page
page-navigation: false   # suppress the strip on this page only
---
```

The doc-level value takes precedence over `website.page-navigation`
and the project top-level setting.

### How prev/next are chosen

When the strip is enabled, Quarto walks the **sidebar** that contains
the current page and picks the immediately-adjacent entries:

- The sidebar is flattened depth-first, with section headers
  (`section: …`) taking part in the sequence iff they have an `href`
  of their own.
- Duplicate entries (same `href` appearing more than once) are
  collapsed to the first occurrence before adjacency is computed.
- A `--- ` separator is a hard boundary: a page sitting next to a
  separator gets `None` on that side, never the entry past the
  separator.

A page that doesn't appear in any sidebar gets no strip — even when
`page-navigation: true` is set. The same is true if the strip would be
empty on both sides (a "lonely" page).

### When to leave it off

Sites built around a navbar and a few top-level pages (like a
brochure or a small docs landing page) usually don't benefit from
prev/next. The Quarto 1 default of `false` for websites reflects
that. Turn it on when you have a meaningful linear reading order —
typically a sidebar with a curated sequence of pages.

## Page footer

The `page-footer:` key controls the footer. Its simplest form is a string
that becomes the centered footer text:

``` yaml
page-footer: "Copyright 2026, Acme Co."
```

To split the footer into regions, use the object form:

``` yaml
page-footer:
  left: "Copyright 2026, **Acme** Co."
  right:
    - icon: github
      href: https://github.com/
```

### Footer options

| Option       | Description                                                                                           |
|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `left`       | Content for the left region: a string (markdown in document context) or a list of navigation items.   |
| `center`     | Same shape, for the center region.                                                                    |
| `right`      | Same shape, for the right region.                                                                     |
| `border`     | `true`, `false`, or a color. Controls the top border.                                                 |
| `background` | Background color.                                                                                     |
| `foreground` | Foreground color.                                                                                     |

As with the navbar, `page-footer: false` suppresses the footer.

## Navigation items

Items used in `navbar.left`, `navbar.right`, dropdown menus, and footer
regions all share the same shape. A bare string is shorthand for an `href`:

``` yaml
left:
  - about.qmd                              # shorthand: { href: about.qmd }
  - text: Home                             # explicit form
    href: index.qmd
  - text: Docs                             # dropdown menu
    menu:
      - text: Getting Started
        href: start.qmd
      - text: Reference
        href: ref.qmd
```

Supported keys on a navigation item:

| Key          | Description                                                                                     |
|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `href`       | Target URL or project-relative path. Can also be written as `file:` for clarity.                |
| `text`       | Display text. In document context this is rendered as markdown.                                 |
| `icon`       | Bootstrap icon name (e.g. `github`, `bluesky`); see <https://icons.getbootstrap.com/>.          |
| `aria-label` | Accessibility label for the link.                                                               |
| `rel`        | HTML `rel` attribute.                                                                           |
| `target`     | HTML `target` attribute (e.g. `_blank` to open in a new tab).                                   |
| `menu`       | Nested list of navigation items. Makes the entry a dropdown; usually has no `href` of its own.  |

## Markdown in text fields

In document frontmatter, string values are interpreted as markdown by
default (this is a general property of Quarto 2's metadata handling, not
specific to navigation). Writing

``` yaml
page-footer:
  left: "Copyright 2026, **Acme** Co."
```

in a document's frontmatter produces `Copyright 2026, <strong>Acme</strong> Co.`
in the rendered footer. In `_quarto.yml`, strings are kept literal by
default; opt in to markdown with the `!md` tag:

``` yaml
page-footer:
  left: !md "Copyright 2026, **Acme** Co."
```

Use `!str` if you want a literal string in document context.

## Controlling merges with `!prefer` and `!concat`

Navbar and page-footer settings follow the usual metadata-merge rules:

- **Scalars** (e.g. `background`, `title`): last layer wins. Setting
  `navbar: { background: secondary }` in a document overrides a project-
  level `background: primary`.
- **Arrays** (e.g. `left`, `right`): default merge is `!concat`, i.e.
  document items are appended to project items.
- **Maps**: by default, keys are deep-merged; the higher layer's scalars
  replace the lower layer's, but sibling keys from the lower layer survive.

To change this per-value, use the `!prefer` tag to reset/replace, or
`!concat` to make concatenation explicit:

``` yaml
# _quarto.yml
navbar:
  left:
    - index.qmd
    - about.qmd

# doc.qmd — replace the entire `left` array:
navbar:
  left: !prefer [special.qmd]

# doc.qmd — append to the project's `left` array (explicit):
navbar:
  left: !concat [extra.qmd]
```

The affirmative-disable shortcut `navbar: false` / `page-footer: false`
works without any special tag: because scalars default to last-wins, the
`false` in a document's frontmatter overrides a full navbar/footer object
in the project layer.
